title: How creams work, and a clean, safe workspace
course_title: Natural Skincare: Basic Creams, Lotions and Facial Oils

say: How creams work, and a clean, safe workspace.
This is the video for module one of Natural Skincare.
If you make whipped shea butter or body oils, you make anhydrous products. Anhydrous means without water. A facial oil is like that. It needs no preservative, but the oils can go rancid.
Creams and lotions are mostly water, held together with oil. That smooth mixture is called an emulsion. The moment a product contains water, bacteria, yeast and mould can grow in it.
So a broad-spectrum preservative, one that works against all three, is not optional.
A badly made butter usually just feels grainy. But an unpreserved cream can grow germs that customers cannot see or smell.

panel.heading: A cream is a step up in responsibility
items: A bad butter just feels grainy
A bad cream can grow hidden germs
Customers rub it on their face

say: And then they rub it onto their face. So treat every water-based product as one that must be made cleanly, preserved properly, and tested before anyone else uses it.

say: Every cream has the same building blocks. The water phase is the biggest part: distilled water, plus glycerin, which draws moisture to the skin. Never use tap, borehole, sachet or bottled water. Their minerals can shorten shelf life.

panel.heading: The building blocks of a lotion
items: Emulsifying wax, melted with the oils

say: The oil phase holds your oils and butters. Light oils give a thin feel, butters make it richer.

panel.heading: The building blocks of a lotion
items: Emulsifying wax, melted with the oils

say: The emulsifying wax holds oil and water together. Ordinary beeswax is not an emulsifier. Beeswax and water recipes often separate.

panel.heading: The building blocks of a lotion
items: Emulsifying wax, melted with the oils

say: The cool-down phase holds the preservative, which goes in after cooling, because heat can damage it.

panel.heading: The building blocks of a lotion
items: Emulsifying wax, melted with the oils

say: For example, Amaka in Enugu finds a simple lotion formula on Humblebee and Me, a respected formulation blog. Distilled water 76.5 percent, vegetable glycerin 10 percent. That is the water phase.
Emulsifying Wax NF 3 percent, and fractionated coconut oil 10 percent. That is the oil phase.
And Liquid Germall Plus, a preservative, at 0.5 percent, in the cool-down.
She adds them up, and they total 100.

Then she checks the essentials. A named emulsifier, and a named broad-spectrum preservative. If a recipe has water but no real emulsifier or no preservative, it is not ready to make for other people, however beautiful the video looks.

panel.heading: Amaka reads a published formula
panel.rule: Every formula must add up to 100 percent.

say: Cleaning removes dirt and grease. Sanitising kills most germs that remain. You need both, in that order, because dirt protects germs. Wash every tool in hot water with dish soap.

panel.heading: Your hygiene routine, every batch
items: Wash tools in hot soapy water, rinse
Dry fully on a clean rack or paper towel
Clean the surface, then sanitise it
Spray tools and jars with 70% alcohol
Wash hands, gloves on, spray gloves

say: Dry them fully, not with a shared kitchen cloth.

say: Spray tools, jars, lids and the blender head with 70 percent isopropyl alcohol. 70 works better than 100, because its water helps kill germs. If you only find 99 percent, Bisi's method is 354 ml topped up with distilled water to 500 ml.

say: Isopropyl alcohol is highly flammable. Never spray it near a gas flame, and let it evaporate fully before you switch on heat.

panel.rule: Let the alcohol dry fully before any heat goes on.

say: You will heat wax and water to about 75 degrees Celsius. That can cause serious burns. Use oven gloves, keep handles turned inward, keep children out of the kitchen, and never leave a pot on heat unattended, even if the power goes off.

cards.d: Wax and water at 75°C burn. Use oven gloves, turn handles inward, never leave a pot unattended.
Cool under cool running water for 20 minutes. Get medical help for large or deep burns.
Keep cables away from the water bath. Unplug the blender before touching the blade.

say: If hot wax or oil touches skin, cool it under cool running water for 20 minutes, and seek medical help for large or deep burns.

say: Before you turn on the heat, tick every item. Tools washed and dried. Surfaces and tools sanitised. Hair covered and gloves on. Formula printed. A scale that reads to 0.01 g, because 0.5 percent of a 200 g batch is just 1 g. And children and pets out.
To remember. Water in a product always means a broad-spectrum preservative. Beeswax is not an emulsifier. Use distilled water only.
Clean first, then sanitise. And let alcohol dry before heat, and never leave the pot.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Water in a product means a preservative
Clean first, then sanitise with 70% alcohol
